newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says ready to discuss freeing more Iraq POWs.
newsitem.headline: Iran says ready to discuss freeing more Iraq POWs.

text.p: A senior Iranian official said his country was ready to continue negotiations with its former foe Iraq on freeing prisoners of war after Tehran released more than 700 POWs, a newspaper said on Sunday.

"After the recent visit of an Iraqi delegation to Tehran, the (Iranian) Commission (in charge of prisoners of war) announced its readiness to continue talks," Brigadier General Abdollah Najafi said in an interview with the daily Iran. He gave no details of the visit.
"We hope the Iraqi side will prepare the ground in the shortest possible amount of time for the return home of Iranian POWs," he said.
Baghdad said on Saturday that Tehran had freed 722 POWs from the 1980-1988 Iran-Iraq war while Najafi said 724 people had been freed.

Iran said it released the POWs, including 24 Christians, in the presence of representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross. Both sides have exchanged several hundred POWs and remains of soldiers. Iraq has said in the past that Iran was still holding 20,000 Iraqi POWs.
Accounting for POWs and soldiers missing in action is among the thorniest issues hindering efforts to improve ties.

"Latest information indicates that the Iraqi attitude towards POWs has improved," Najafi told the Iran newspaper. "We expect the POW problem will be resolved soon for humanitarian reasons as well as for the improvement of mutual relations."
